name: cfd_run_reactor_experiment
description:
Run a complete reactor experiment and return the physical result. This is the
tool to use: it chains import -> flow -> mixing -> reaction as ONE request, and
derives every file the solver needs from the chosen mesh. Nothing here is a
server-side path.

CHOOSE A REACTOR by id from the enum (cfd_list_reactors describes each, with its
inlet count and whether it can dose two reactants separately). Reaction: either
the simple form -- concentration_a_mol_per_m3, concentration_b_mol_per_m3 and
rate_constant_m3_per_mol_s for A + B -> C -- or the general form, mechanism plus
inlet_feeds. Everything else has a default.

DERIVED FROM THE MESH, never asked for: the zone names and their roles, the
fluid volume, the inlet areas, the throughput, the residence time
tau = V / Q, the time step, all four step budgets, the checkpoint stride and the
mesh fingerprint. The step budgets are sized so the run covers `turnovers`
flow-through times; the default 4 is the smallest value that reliably clears the
3-turnover gate below.

WHICH WAY TO STEP, measured on these meshes:
* Conversion too low? Raise rate_constant_m3_per_mol_s or the concentrations
  first. Lowering inlet_speed_m_per_s also works -- it raises the residence time
  in proportion -- but it lengthens the solve by the same factor.
* Do NOT reach for species_diffusivity_m2_s. On a mesh of this resolution the
  numerical diffusion from the advection scheme (about u*h/2, measured at
  5.7e-6 m^2/s at 0.15 m/s) dominates any liquid-phase value: raising D by 100x
  changed conversion by 0.75%, while raising the rate constant by 100x changed
  it 89-fold. A conversion that only appears at large D is a mesh artifact.
* Damkohler is the dial to watch: below ~0.1 the mixture leaves before reacting,
  above ~10 it finishes well inside the reactor. Aim for 1-10. Note the cost is
  not symmetric - a case at Da ~2 solved in 6 minutes while the same case at
  ~200 had not finished in 110.
* Flow not converging? Lower inlet_speed_m_per_s. Cost measured on ss316:
  0.15 m/s needed 11,556 steps (4.7 h), 0.02 m/s needed 2,850 (1.3 h).

TWO THINGS THAT INVALIDATE A RESULT rather than merely degrade it. A run
covering under 3 residence times reports a conversion near zero that means
'the domain is still filling', not 'the reaction does not proceed' - raise
turnovers, and `blocking` carries the value to use. And a flow stage that
stopped at its step ceiling is refused by the reaction stage outright.

RETURNS 'results' (the physical values: pressure_drop_pa across the reactor,
residence_time_s, damkohler, conversion_by_reactant, outlet concentrations,
mixing index), 'derived' (everything computed from the mesh), 'trustworthy'
(the chain's weakest verdict) and 'blocking' (what stands in the way, tagged
with the stage that found it).

wait_seconds bounds how long THIS CALL blocks, not the experiment. On expiry the tool returns status='pending' with the request_id rather than raising, because an MCP client's own request timeout is far shorter than a converging flow solve and an exception would read as a failed experiment. Pass 0 to return immediately. Either way, fetch the outcome later with cfd_get_experiment_result(request_id). request_id is a caller-owned idempotency key. While the run is in flight, and afterwards for as long as the service still holds a succeeded or cancelled record of it, reusing it returns that same run instead of starting a second one; reusing it with different arguments is rejected. A run that failed is not replayed - reusing its request_id deliberately starts a fresh run. Records are capped and evicted oldest-first and are lost on restart, so a request_id reused long after its run finished may start a fresh run.

name: cfd_get_experiment_result
description: Fetch a reactor experiment by request_id. Use it after cfd_run_reactor_experiment returned status='pending' because its wait expired, or any time later to re-read a finished one. status='pending' means the chain is still running - keep polling; 'succeeded', 'failed' and 'cancelled' are terminal. The payload is identical to what a waiting run returns: 'results', 'derived', 'trustworthy', 'blocking' and a per-stage breakdown.

name: cfd_list_reactors
description: List the reactor geometries this deployment carries. Each entry gives the id to pass to cfd_run_reactor_experiment, the cell count and mesh size, the named inlets, outlets and walls, and 'supports_two_reactant_feed' - false for a single-inlet geometry, which cannot dose two reactants separately and so cannot host an A + B reaction. 'available: false' means the mesh file is not on this host.

name: cfd_list_artifacts
description: Page through local artifacts produced by a run.

description: Stop a running local solver subprocess.
